findings.claim: Play-test step 6 ('Tap RETRY, then NEXT RACE') fails on the phone viewport. A six-car race now always shows a 6-row results table. At 844×390, the project's reference frame, the centred results column overflows: RETRY and NEXT RACE are pushed below the bottom edge and the track title is clipped at the top. The layer can't scroll (body has overflow: hidden and touch-action: none), so the owner can't tap the buttons. Before B04, player races had only 2 rows.
findings.evidence: Screenshot /inputs/screenshots/844x390/stage/results--podium.png (6 rows, the same count every six-car race now produces): the table fills the screen from y≈75 to y≈370, and only the top ~5px of the RETRY and NEXT RACE buttons show at y≈385. The 'BRAMBLE BENDS' title is cut off at the top. Layout: overlay() in src/ui/dom.ts:69 builds 'ui-layer ui-screen ui-results'. .ui-layer is position:absolute; inset:0 (components.css:23). .ui-screen centres with flex and has no overflow or scroll (screens.css:3-7). .ui-results is a flex column with gap s5 (screens.css:10-17), and body in base.css:9 has overflow:hidden. The rows have gap s2 (results.css:66-70), so stripes + label + track + 7 row-heights + actions exceed 390px. Trace: tap RACE → src/game.ts onRace passes carCount: PLAYER_CAR_COUNT (6) → finish → results.show builds 6 rows (results-screen.ts:111) → buttons are off-screen at 844×390. The 1440×900 stage fits.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the results screen fit six rows at 844×390. For example, at short viewports put the actions beside the table or tighten the column gaps and row padding (tokens only), so the stripes, title, 6 rows and RETRY/NEXT RACE all fit within 390px. Check results--podium at 844x390 afterwards.

findings.claim: With six cars every race started from RACE/RETRY/NEXT RACE ends on a 6-row results screen that does not fit the 844×390 phone viewport. The content needs about 491px in a 357px box, is centred so it is clipped at both ends, and the page cannot scroll. RETRY and NEXT RACE start at y≈385 of 390, a sliver of about 5px, and pause is disabled after the finish, so a phone player cannot leave the results screen.
findings.evidence: Reference viewport 844×390. results-screen.ts:62-73 stacks [stripes+label+title] / [roundel+best chip | table] / [RETRY, NEXT RACE] in one column. .ui-screen centres it (screens.css:3-7). html, body have overflow:hidden; touch-action:none (base.css:2-13), so nothing scrolls. A row is .ui-value 28px + 2×4 padding + 2×3 border = 42px with 8px gaps (results.css:67-77). Six rows make a 330px table (header and gap included). Column = 77 (title block) + 16 + 330 + 16 + 52 (button) = 491px, versus 390 − 12 (--safe-top) − 21 (--safe-bottom) = 357px. About 134px overflows, split over both ends. Screenshot screenshots/844x390/stage/results--podium.png (6 racers): 'BRAMBLE BENDS' is cut at the top, stripes and label are above y=0, and the buttons' tops are at y≈385. With 2 racers (race/bends-finished.png) the buttons sit at y≈303–355 and everything fits. The mockup guardrails/design/mockups/S5-results.png fits 6 rows plus both buttons in 844×390. The gate race screenshots only show 2 rows because the protected driver starts 2-car races. Before B04 a real race had 2 rows; now every one has 6. Pause is ignored once the player has finished (game.ts:166). The spec play-test steps 5-6 ('tap RETRY, then NEXT RACE') cannot be done on a phone. The AC7 UI test passes only because happy-dom has no layout.
findings.suggestedFix: Lay the screen out as in mockup S5, in results-screen.ts and results.css. Put the stripes full width on top. Put label, track name, roundel and best-lap chip in the left column. Put the table and then the RETRY / NEXT RACE row in the right column. Make rows about 32-36px (type at --type-button-size, tighter row padding and gap, tokens only) so that 6 rows + header + buttons fit the 357px content box. Scrolling is not an option because body is overflow:hidden and touch-action:none.

findings.claim: startRace() sets menuTrack before raceDrivers() can throw on an invalid carCount. A rejected call therefore still switches the track that the RACE button and the next startRace() use, and that GameState.trackId reports.
findings.evidence: game.ts:236-238: `const track = getTrack(options.trackId ?? menuTrack.id); menuTrack = track; const drivers = raceDrivers(options.carCount ?? DEFAULT_CAR_COUNT);`. raceDrivers throws 'a race has 1..6 cars, got 7' for carCount 7, 0 or 2.5 (src/content/drivers.ts:25-27). Steps: createGame (menu, menuTrack = TRACKS[0] = bends, because tracks are sorted by file name). Then `expect(() => game.startRace({ trackId: 'dust-bowl', carCount: 7 })).toThrow()` passes, and `game.state().trackId` is now 'dust-bowl' (was 'bends'). No race started and the start screen still says Bramble Bends, yet game.startRace() and the RACE button now start Dust Bowl. Before this diff carCount was the constant DRIVERS.length, so nothing after `menuTrack = track` could fail on input; the new throw point is introduced here.
findings.suggestedFix: Move `menuTrack = track;` below the raceDrivers(...) and createWorld(...) calls, just before `race = {`, so a failed start leaves the menu state untouched.

findings.claim: The start screen subtitle is built once at createGame from the initial menuTrack, but menuTrack changes on every startRace (NEXT RACE moves to the next track). After NEXT RACE → QUIT TO MENU the start screen still shows the old track name and lap count while RACE starts the new track. This predates B04, but sits in the createStartScreen options literal whose onRace line this diff edits.
findings.evidence: game.ts:137-140: `createStartScreen(menuLayer, { onRace: () => game.startRace({ trackId: menuTrack.id, carCount: PLAYER_CAR_COUNT }), subtitle: `${menuTrack.name} · ${menuTrack.laps} laps` })`. The subtitle is a string evaluated once; showMenu() (game.ts:264-268) only calls startScreen.show() and never refreshes it. src/ui/start-screen.ts renders the text once and exposes no setter. Steps: boot, subtitle 'Bramble Bends · 2 laps' (TRACKS[0] = bends). RACE, finish, NEXT RACE (nextTrackId gives dust-bowl, menuTrack = dust-bowl). Pause, QUIT TO MENU. The start screen still reads 'Bramble Bends · 2 laps'; pressing RACE starts Dust Bowl, 3 laps. Test: `game.startRace({ trackId: 'dust-bowl', seed: 1 }); game.showMenu(); expect(root.querySelector('.ui-start__subtitle')?.textContent).toBe('Dust Bowl · 3 laps')` fails (still 'Bramble Bends · 2 laps').
findings.suggestedFix: Let the start screen update its subtitle: make createStartScreen always render the subtitle node and return setSubtitle(text), then call it from showMenu() with the current menuTrack. Use the singular 'lap' for 1 lap, as results-screen.ts:106 does.

findings.claim: The diff adds two near-identical copies of `playerInputs(trackId, seed)`, one in each new test file. Both also re-implement `botsFor` (one bot per car), which already exists in tests/sim/helpers.ts:62.
findings.suggestedFix: Import `botsFor` from '../sim/helpers.ts' in both files instead of mapping `createBot` inline. Better still, put a single `twinPlayerInputs(trackId, seed, carCount, maxTicks)` in a new tests/game/helpers.ts (new files under tests/ are allowed) built on `botsFor`, and call it from both six-car test files. Each file then loses its local copy.

findings.claim: The spec requires the cached scene to be rebuilt when the driver list changes, not only when the track changes. No test covers this. Every game test mocks createRaceScene with a stub that ignores its liveries argument, so reverting the cache key to track-only passes every test, even though the real scene would then have only 2 car meshes for a 6-car race.
findings.evidence: Mutation: in src/game.ts:82 change `const key = `${world.track.data.id}|${drivers.length}`;` to `const key = world.track.data.id;`. That makes it equivalent to the old `sceneTrack` check. No test fails. tests/game/six-car-grid.test.ts:9-12 and six-car-race.test.ts:10-13 both mock `createRaceScene: () => ({ update() {}, ... })` and never check how many times it was called or what it was called with. In the real game the steps are: `startRace({ trackId: 'dust-bowl' })`, which is 2 cars by default (e.g. via window.__racer), then RACE on the start screen on the same track, which is 6 cars. sceneFor reuses the 2-livery scene. In src/render/scene.ts:149 `for (let i = 0; i < cars.length; i++)` loops only over the 2 meshes, so cars 2–5 are simulated and shown on the minimap but never drawn.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a test in a new file (e.g. tests/game/six-car-scene.test.ts) that mocks createRaceScene with `vi.fn((_layout, liveries) => ({ ...stub }))`. Call `game.startRace({ trackId: T })`, then `game.startRace({ trackId: T, carCount: 6 })`, and assert that the mock was called again and its last call's liveries have length 6. Also assert that restarting with the same count reuses the scene: no new call, and reset() is called.

fixes.summary:
The finding was real. At 844×390 the six-row results screen put the 'Bramble Bends' title at y=-7 and RETRY / NEXT RACE at y=384–436. I rearranged the results layout to match the S5 mockup, using tokens only.
- src/ui/results-screen.ts: the triple stripe is now a direct child of the screen. The left column holds the label, track title, placing roundel and best-lap chip. The right column (`ui-results__side`) holds the results table with the RETRY / NEXT RACE actions under it.
- src/ui/results.css: the stripe is now an edge-to-edge 4:2:1 band in the 12px top inset (absolutely positioned, height s3, built like the pause card's band). The right column is right-aligned with gap s4. Gaps between rows go from s2 to s1, and rows use type-button-size instead of hud-l, as in the mockup.
Six rows plus the buttons now fit within 390px. The screenshots at 844×390 (win and podium) and 1440×900 look right next to the mockup. No behaviour, roles or DOM hooks used by tests changed.
New test tests/ui/results-fit-phone.test.ts builds the harness screens bundle and renders the results--podium stage (six racers) in Chromium at 844×390. It checks that the stripes, title, all header and data rows, and both buttons are inside the viewport. It failed before the fix (title top -6.9, buttons bottom 435.9) and passes after. pnpm typecheck passes and pnpm test passes (76 files, 599 tests).

In src/game.ts startRace(), I moved `menuTrack = track;` from straight after getTrack() to below the raceDrivers(...), createWorld(...) and carViews(...) calls, just before `race = {`. Now a call that raceDrivers rejects (carCount 7, 0, 2.5) throws before any menu state changes. state().trackId, the RACE button and the next default startRace() all keep the previous menu track. Valid starts behave exactly as before because the assignment still happens before anything reads menuTrack. New test tests/game/start-race-invalid-count.test.ts is the verifier's test plus a check that mode stays 'menu'. It failed before the fix (expected 'dust-bowl' to be 'bends') and passes after it. pnpm typecheck is clean and pnpm test passes: 77 files, 600 tests.

Removed the duplicated playerInputs helpers. tests/game/six-car-race.test.ts and tests/game/six-car-grid.test.ts are both new in tonight's diff, so editing them is allowed. Added a new tests/game/helpers.ts that exports twinPlayerInputs(trackId, seed, carCount, maxTicks). It is built on the existing botsFor from tests/sim/helpers.ts, so neither file maps createBot inline any more. It runs the same loop as before (bot inputs for car 0 of a twin world, stepped until car 0 finishes or maxTicks is reached) and keeps the grid file's check that car 0 finished. Both files now call it, with FIVE_MINUTES in the race test and TEN_MINUTES (the old 60*60*10) in the grid test. Their local copies and the unused imports (createBot, stepWorld, CarInput, getTrack) are gone. The one change in behaviour is that the race test now also checks the twin's car 0 finished, which its AC5 test already requires, so no outcome changes. No src/ changes. pnpm typecheck passes, and pnpm test passes: 77 files and 600 tests, including all 10 six-car tests. This is a duplication fix, so there is no red/green test. ESLint couldn't be run in the sandbox because it isn't installed locally and there's no network.
